questions.prompt: Rosie has some tiles on a board with these numbers on them: 21, 32, 75, 46, 143, 88, 200, 134, 56, 97. Each tile has a number on it. How many of these numbers are odd?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers are 21, 75, 143 and 97 — 4 in total.

questions.prompt: Cai wrote down this number pattern: 97, 93, ?, 85, 81. What number should ? be?
questions.explanation: The pattern decreases by 4 each time: 97, 93, 89, 85, 81.

questions.prompt: Which of these numbers has its largest digit in the tens column?
questions.explanation: 283 has 8 in the tens place — the largest tens digit among the four numbers.

questions.prompt: Five students are standing in a park, as shown: Ted → Mark → Sue are in a line, with Adam and Jack elsewhere in the park. Mark is facing Sue. Who is standing behind Mark?
questions.explanation: Mark is facing Sue, so the person on Mark's other side — Ted — is standing behind him.

questions.prompt: Kimi decided to start fishing at the morning high tide. She looked up the tide times for Monday 6 June. At what time should Kimi start fishing?
questions.explanation: The morning high tide is at 9:01 am.

questions.prompt: Lulu asked 12 friends what they had for lunch and recorded the results as a dot plot. Two more friends had rice than salad. Which column shows the number of friends who had salad?
questions.explanation: Column A (2 dots) is exactly 2 less than column B (4 dots), matching "two more had rice than salad."

questions.prompt: Toma had this card. Which of these cards is identical to Toma's card?
questions.explanation: Option C is a diamond matching Toma's card in both size and shape. Options A and B are diamonds of the wrong size, and option D is an upright square, not a diamond at all.

questions.prompt: What is the mass shown on the scale?
questions.explanation: The needle points three-quarters of the way between the 3 kg and 4 kg marks, at 3.75 kg.

questions.prompt: Which of these is almost certain to happen? (A) Jim tosses a coin and it lands on heads. (B) Sasi turns the page on the calendar from Thursday 15th and the next day is Friday. (C) Mary flicks a 4-section spinner and it lands on 3. (D) Harry picks the green jellybean from a small mixed handful without looking.

options.label: A
options.text: Jim tosses a coin and it lands on heads.

options.label: B
options.text: Sasi turns the page and the next day is Friday.

options.label: C

questions.explanation: The day after Thursday is always Friday — this is certain, unlike the coin toss (1/2), the spinner (1/4) or picking one particular jellybean from a handful.

questions.prompt: Lani drew three hexagons on triangular grid paper and shaded them green, as shown. How many triangles did Lani shade?
questions.explanation: Each hexagon is made up of 12 small triangles on this grid. 3 hexagons × 12 = 36.

questions.prompt: Which of these pictures shows 1¾ shaded squares?
questions.explanation: One whole square plus three quarters of a second square shaded = 1¾.

questions.prompt: The entrance to Emma's house is 200 metres from the entrance to Jane's house, as shown on the map. What does 1 unit on the map represent?
questions.explanation: The houses are 4 grid units apart on the map, and 4 units = 200 m, so 1 unit = 50 m.

questions.prompt: To obtain the number in each hexagon, Holly multiplied the numbers in the two hexagons directly below it. What are the values of P, Q and R?

Gina had a compass. She followed these directions in order: turn west and walk 10 metres; turn north and walk 20 metres; turn east and walk 40 metres; turn south and walk 20 metres. How far was Gina from her starting point?
questions.explanation: North and south cancel out (20 − 20 = 0). East and west combine to a net 30 m east (40 − 10 = 30).

questions.prompt: Toby had a playlist with 6 songs, with lengths shown in the table. He played the songs in order from the start of Song 1, without pausing. Which song was playing exactly 7 minutes after Toby started the playlist?
questions.explanation: Song 1 and 2 finish by 4:20 (260 s). Song 3 then plays until 7:10 (430 s) — 7:00 (420 s) falls inside that window.

questions.prompt: Where is 0.7 on this number line, which runs from 0.4 to 0.8?
questions.explanation: 0.7 sits three-quarters of the way from 0.4 to 0.8, matching the point marked C.

questions.prompt: Janice drew this shape. She rotated it anticlockwise by a quarter of a turn. Which of these shows the shape after this rotation?
questions.explanation: Rotating the shape 90° anticlockwise moves the red half from the right side to the top, and the dotted green half from the left side to the bottom, matching option A.

questions.prompt: Which two numbers differ by 43?

There are 9 marbles in a bag: 1 blue, 3 green, 2 red and 3 yellow. Tom took out a green marble, leaving 8 marbles in the bag. Then it was Julie's turn to take out a marble without looking. Which two colours does Julie have the same chance of taking out?
questions.explanation: After removing a green marble, there are 2 green and 2 red marbles left — equal chances.

questions.prompt: In a small wildlife park, one-quarter of the animals are snakes and the rest are lizards or birds. There are 70 snakes in the wildlife park. How many lizards and birds are there?
questions.explanation: Total animals = 70 × 4 = 280. Lizards and birds = 280 − 70 = 210.

questions.prompt: Lin made a solid using five cubes. Which of these is NOT a possible view of Lin's solid?
questions.explanation: Option B shows a different arrangement of cubes than Lin's original solid, so it cannot be a rotated view of the same solid.

questions.prompt: Ardi, Priya and Raj took turns to paint their house. Painting began at 7 am and finished at 11 pm without a break. Priya painted for one-quarter of the time. Ardi painted for the same amount of time as Raj. How long did Raj spend painting the house?
questions.explanation: 7 am to 11 pm is 16 hours. Priya painted 1/4 × 16 = 4 hours, leaving 12 hours split evenly between Ardi and Raj: 6 hours each.

questions.prompt: Emma is making a pattern of diamonds using small triangles, as shown. Shape 1 uses 2 triangles, Shape 2 uses 8 triangles, Shape 3 uses 18 triangles. How many small triangles will she need to make the 4th shape in her pattern?
questions.explanation: Each shape uses 2n² triangles: 2(1)²=2, 2(2)²=8, 2(3)²=18, so Shape 4 needs 2(4)² = 32.

questions.prompt: Lynne cut a rectangular piece out of a patterned square, as shown. Which of these is the cut-out piece?
questions.explanation: Option B has the diagonal plaid pattern aligned to match the gap exactly, in both direction and position.

questions.prompt: There are 12 animal signs in the Chinese calendar. They repeat every 12 years in the same order. For example, people born in 1955 or 1967 were born in the 'Year of the Goat' (1955: Goat, 1956: Monkey, 1957: Rooster, 1958: Dog). Cai turned 35 on 20 April 2017. In which 'Year' was he born?
questions.explanation: Cai was born in 1982. 1982 − 1955 = 27, and 27 mod 12 = 3, the same position in the cycle as 1958 — Year of the Dog.

questions.prompt: Freya left this note with directions to her house. Which house is Freya's?
questions.explanation: Tracing the directions from the school along McDonald Street and the three turns leads to house C.

questions.prompt: Josh wants to make a quilt for his bed using a number of 20 cm × 20 cm squares. The rectangular quilt must cover his bed, measuring 80 cm by 200 cm, and have an extra 20 cm on all four sides. How many squares does Josh need to make the quilt?
questions.explanation: The quilt is 120 cm × 240 cm (adding 20 cm on each side). That's 6 × 12 = 72 squares of 20 cm.

questions.prompt: Fadi only had from 3:40 pm until 5:25 pm to see a movie with his friends. Fadi and his friends watched one complete movie together. Which movie did they watch?
questions.explanation: Only the 4:05 pm showing of Flying Home starts after Fadi arrives (3:40 pm) and finishes (5:25 pm) by the time he must leave.

questions.prompt: Debbie used the digits 4, 7 and 8 to make 2-digit numbers. For example, 47 and 88 were two of the nine numbers that Debbie made. How many of these 2-digit numbers are divisible by 3?
questions.explanation: Numbers whose digits sum to a multiple of 3: 48, 78, 84 and 87 — 4 numbers.

questions.prompt:
★ − 12 = ◆
◆ + ◆ + ◆ = ★ + ★
What is the value of ★?
questions.explanation: From the first equation, ◆ = ★ − 12. Substituting into the second: 3(★ − 12) = 2★, giving 3★ − 36 = 2★, so ★ = 36.

questions.prompt: There are 24 students in Mr Sim's class. Four students play two sports each; all other students play only one sport. One-quarter of the students play tennis. How many students play basketball, given the table of sports played?
questions.explanation: 24 students playing one sport each = 28 total "plays" (24 + 4 who play two). Tennis is one-quarter of 24 = 6. 6+8+5 = 19, so basketball = 28 − 19 = 9.

questions.prompt: Dani is a baker. She started with 1 gram of yeast. The amount of yeast doubled every 12 hours. How much yeast was there after 48 hours?
questions.explanation: 48 hours is 4 doubling periods: 1 × 2⁴ = 16 grams.

questions.prompt: Aditya had this tangled piece of wool. He cut the wool into 7 pieces using one straight cut. Which of the following diagrams shows the path Aditya took to cut the wool?
questions.explanation: A single straight cut needs to cross the wool exactly 7 times to create 7 pieces — option D's line crosses the tangled strand more than any of the other paths.

In this addition, ▲ and ★ represent digits:
  ▲ ★
  ★ 7
+ 1 ▲

1 0 ★
What are the values of ▲ and ★?

Mike makes advertising signs. The length is always twice the height. The most popular size is 6 m long and 3 m high. A customer wants Mike to make a sign with a perimeter of 42 metres. What are the dimensions of this sign?
questions.explanation: With height h and length 2h, perimeter = 2(h + 2h) = 6h = 42, so h = 7 and length = 14.

questions.prompt: Raj went shopping. On Monday he spent half of his money. On Tuesday he spent one-quarter of his remaining money. He was left with $18. How much money did Raj begin with?
questions.explanation: After Monday, half remains. After Tuesday, 3/4 of that remains: 3/4 × 1/2 × x = 18, so x = 48.

questions.prompt: Carol is making greeting cards using these two images. Each image is placed the same way up, in one of four positions in a 2×2 grid, and each image is used exactly twice. How many different greeting cards can Carol make?
questions.explanation: Choosing 2 of the 4 grid positions for the first image determines the whole layout: C(4,2) = 6 arrangements.

questions.prompt: Four luggage bags were weighed together in different combinations, shown in the table. What was the total mass of bag 1 and bag 3?

There are 48 boxes of tissues in a carton. Inside each box are 100 tissues. Each person, in an office of 50 people, uses an average of 3 tissues per day. How long would it take these 50 people to use 9 cartons of tissues?
questions.explanation: 9 cartons = 9 × 48 × 100 = 43 200 tissues. 50 people use 150 tissues per day. 43 200 ÷ 150 = 288 days.

questions.prompt: Lien folded this net to make a 12-sided dice. He placed it on the table so that 12 was showing on top. Which face was on the bottom?
questions.explanation: Tracing the net's fold pattern, the pentagon labelled B ends up directly opposite the face labelled 12.
